subject: Tier lockback interpretation & pricing exhibit amendment
messages:
From: Emma Shaw <emma.shaw@novahealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement Ops <procurement@novahealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Draft redline for pricing exhibit — interpretation ask

Hi Logan / Marissa,

Thanks again for the call this morning. We attached a redline of Exhibit A to the Master Order (Nova_Pricing_EA_redline.docx) with three asks that need alignment before we move to procurement sign-off:

1) Tier lockback (Section 2.3): Our legal team is reading this as a hard lock that prevents any reallocation of committed SKUs between tiers for the duration of the year. We think that blocks our planned mid-year pack migration to support seasonal volume. Can Redwood consider language that allows a one-time pack migration subject to a true-up?

2) Floor reset language: The floor reset in 2.5 looks like an automatic annual reset that could materially increase our minimum spend after year one. We need clarity on whether resets are discretionary (mutual) or automatic.

3) Billing mapping / surcharge carveout: We have cases where usage is bursty and should be billed to burst credits rather than committed tiers — need a short operational definition so our billing team can map metrics.

We included inline comments in the attachment. Would you please loop in the appropriate Redwood ops/legal contacts and let us know if the one-time migration + true-up model is feasible?

Attachments: Nova_Pricing_EA_redline.docx (redline), pricing_workbook_example.xlsx (referenced)

Best,
Emma Shaw
Director, Strategic Sourcing
Nova Health

Emma —

Thanks for sending this over and for the clear summary. I appreciate the call — helpful context. I'll loop in Karthik (pricing & sales ops) and Marissa (legal liaison) to review the inline comments and propose language.

High-level response:
- One-time pack migration with a mutually agreeable true-up is something we've done before in similar deals; it usually requires a defined migration window and a reconciliation formula attached as an appendix.
- Floor resets are negotiable; we typically push for mutual agreement but there are cases where an auto-reset tied to a published index was accepted.
- Billing mapping: agree we need an explicit operational definition (metric name + threshold + charge path).

Next step: Karthik / Marissa — can you take lead on a redline set that: (a) allows a single pack migration in year with a reconciliation worksheet, (b) converts the automatic floor-reset to a mutual-review path with an optional indexed reset, and (c) provides a short billing mapping table? Aim to have a draft to Emma by end of week.

Thanks —
Logan Wright
Head of Partnerships
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: RE: Draft redline for pricing exhibit — interpretation ask

Hi all —

I reviewed the redline and Emma's summary. A few operational notes and a proposed approach below; attached my working note (RW_pricing_note.pdf) with an example true-up calculation.

Proposed approach (short):
- Pack migration: Allow one migration per 12-month commitment period. Migration must be requested 30 days in advance, specify SKU mapping, and is subject to a reconciliation that compares actual spend under original tier vs. migrated tier for the remainder of the period. Any shortfall is billed at the higher of (a) migrated tier price, or (b) pro-rata of original committed price — see worksheet.

- Tier lockback wording: Replace absolute "no reallocation" language with "no reallocation except as expressly permitted in Section 4.2 (one-time migration)". This preserves the commercial intent but keeps the door open for the migration path.

- Floor reset: Recommend mutual review rather than automatic reset. If Nova insists on an indexed reset, cap the uptick to +10% YoY and require mutual written consent for anything above that.

- Billing mapping: I propose a 3-row table: metric, threshold, charge path (committed tier / burst credits / overage). We'll include an example where burst credits absorb spikes up to 150% of baseline.

I'll assemble a redline for Exhibit A and the reconciliation appendix — Marissa, can you convert this to clean legal language and produce a one-page summary for procurement? Emma, want your feedback on the 10% cap on resets and the 30-day migration notice.

Attachments: RW_pricing_note.pdf (example calculations)

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Sales Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Shaw <emma.shaw@novahealth.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Draft redline for pricing exhibit — interpretation ask

Emma / Logan / Karthik —

Thanks — I've drafted legal-friendly redline language and appended a short reconciliation appendix. Key changes (see pricing_exhibit_redline_Redwood.docx):

1) Section 2.3 (Tier lockback) — new text: "Except as expressly set forth in Section 4.2 (Permitted Migration), Customer may not reallocate committed SKUs across pricing tiers during a Commitment Period. A single Permitted Migration is allowed per Commitment Period upon 30 days' written notice, subject to the reconciliation methodology in Appendix 1."

2) New Appendix 1 (Migration Reconciliation) — establishes the true-up formula, calculation period, and invoice timing: reconciliation to be completed within 45 days of migration effective date; any shortfall invoiced net 30.

3) Section 2.5 (Floor reset) — converted to "Mutual Review" default with optional indexed reset: if Customer requests an indexed reset, both parties must execute an amendment; any indexed reset cannot exceed a 10% increase to the effective floor without executive sign-off.

4) Billing mapping table inserted as Annex B with operational definitions; final metric names to be agreed in an ops handoff.

Open points for negotiation:
- Nova's procurement asked for the migration to be allowed with a negative true-up in certain operational migration cases (i.e., Redwood absorbs short-term revenue loss to preserve the relationship). Redwood can't accept open-ended absorption, but we can offer a capped absorption (e.g., Redwood covers up to $X or Y% of the shortfall once per term).
- Timing for reconciliation: we propose 45 days; Nova may want 30.

I attached the redline and a short "changes at a glance" file. If Emma is comfortable with the 30-day notice, Appendix 1 reconciliation and the 10% index cap, we can prepare an amendment and DocuSign packet.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Contracts Counsel (Pricing)
Redwood Inference
Attachments: pricing_exhibit_redline_Redwood.docx, summary_of_changes.txt

Marissa / Logan / Karthik —

Appreciate the quick turn. We reviewed your redline and the migration appendix. Nova's position:

- One-time migration with 30 days' notice and the reconciliation formula is acceptable in principle. Procurement has two follow-ups: (a) can Redwood cap the customer's exposure so that in a negative reconciliation, Nova's incremental bill won't exceed a pre-agreed cap (we suggested $75k as a starting point), and (b) can Redwood agree to the 45-day reconciliation timeline (Procurement prefers 30 days but can accept 45 with a penalty-free rollover if reconciliation is delayed).

- On the 10% index cap for floor resets — Nova accepts the cap but asks that any executive sign-off be routable to a Director-level approver rather than C-suite.

- Billing mapping table looks good; our ops team will confirm metric names (we'll send a follow-up spreadsheet).

If you can accept the limited cap on negative true-ups ($75k) and the 45-day timeline with a one-time extension option, Procurement is ready for Redwood to issue an amendment and DocuSign packet. We're attaching the procurement intake: procurement_rfq_2026.pdf and linking a DocuSign placeholder for redline execution: https://docusign.com/ds/placeholder/Nova-RW-ExhibitA

Please advise on the $75k cap and we'll aim to get this into our Q4 procurement run if we close this week.

Best,
